MAPPED the existing PDF chrome via two read-only Explore passes before designing the replacement: hauska-engine has NO html/css rendering pipeline anywhere (grep confirms zero puppeteer/playwright/sharp/resvg in any package.json) -- every PDF is drawn with pdf-lib direct point-based primitives. The 'report-chrome.css' spec therefore has no literal drop-in target; every value must be re-expressed as pdf-lib draw calls and a TS token module, not a CSS file.

FOUND: three report types are produced by three different composers that currently render THREE VISUALLY DIFFERENT headers/footers, including inside the SAME combined document: dossier.ts's drawDossierHeader (reused verbatim by feasibility.ts) draws kicker+address+subline+right-meta+rule; flood-drainage.ts's drawFdHeader is a near-duplicate with an added stats row; render.ts's drawSheetHeader (the site-plan drawing/summary/aerial sheets, used BOTH standalone as the SP- export via author.ts's authorParcelSitePlanExport, AND embedded inside feasibility.ts's combined document) draws a third, condensed-eyebrow style that never matches dossier.ts's style even when both appear back-to-back in one feasibility PDF. This three-way inconsistency -- visible to a customer flipping pages in one document -- is exactly the class of defect 'one frame for all three report types' exists to remove, so scope INCLUDES render.ts's own header/footer, not just the two dossier-style composers.

SCOPE BOUNDARY, decided before editing: the frame is masthead + running header + footer ONLY. Inside render.ts this means drawSheetHeader is replaced, and the FOOTER'S RULE + fine-print band is replaced -- but the legend rows, scale bar, north arrow, drawing, segment table and provenance panel are untouched and simply re-anchored (moved, not re-authored) above the new, shorter footer band, since those are the site-plan sheet's own BODY furniture (per-report-type content), not the generic three-report-type frame the spec governs. No legend label, swatch, order, scale-bar digit or drawing mark changes. This is the falsifier-4 boundary: 'sheet BODY content changes' means values/labels/geometry of the drawing changes, not that its Y-anchor moves when the frame band above/below it changes size.

MASTHEAD-VS-RUNNING-HEADER RULE (needed because render.ts currently draws the SAME full header on all 3 of its own sheets, with no notion of 'first sheet of the document'): masthead draws iff the PRINTED (post-renumbering) sheet number equals 1; every other printed sheet number gets the running header. This is a single rule applied uniformly at all four call sites (dossier cover, feasibility cover, flood-drainage sheet 1, render.ts drawing sheet) -- no per-file special-casing needed, and it automatically produces the correct behavior for every embedding combination already in the repo (e.g. site-plan sheets embedded inside Feasibility never draw a masthead, since Feasibility's own cover is always the document's printed sheet 1).

FONT DECISIONS, each a deliberate substitution, documented here rather than silently: (1) the wordmark's SVG specifies font-family "Oxygen, system-ui, sans-serif" -- a web-font stack whose OWN fallback the designer already wrote for the case Oxygen is unavailable. No Oxygen face is vendored in packages/engine-core/assets/fonts (only Barlow Regular/Medium + Barlow Condensed Medium/SemiBold). Substituting the SAME Barlow Condensed SemiBold already used for every other display/heading role in this PDF system honors that documented fallback chain rather than deviating from it, and avoids vendoring a fifth font file for one static logo string. (2) The spec's mono elements (subject meta, doc-id value, running-header meta, footer meta/timestamp/link/sheet-counter) specify "ui-monospace, SF Mono, Menlo, monospace" -- again a system stack with a generic 'monospace' fallback. Rather than vendor a new TTF, this build uses pdf-lib's built-in standard font Courier (embedded via PDFDocument.embedFont(StandardFonts.Courier/-Bold), no fontkit/TTF required) -- a REAL monospace face, zero new dependency, zero licensing surface, and available with no asset-pipeline risk. (3) The logo ring/ticks/dot geometry is redrawn as pdf-lib vector primitives (drawCircle for the stroked ring and the filled dot, drawLine for the four ticks) at the exact coordinates in logo-mark.svg/logo-wordmark-print.svg, scaled uniformly from each file's native viewBox to its spec display size (20x20 / 175x40) -- no SVG-to-PNG rasterization pipeline exists in this repo (grep: zero sharp/resvg/canvas anywhere) and adding one (native-binary risk) is disproportionate for two small vector marks that are geometrically simple (circle + 4 lines + dot).

TOKEN-FILE DECISION: the spec's instruction to 'port the print tokens into a print-tokens.css alongside pe-tokens.css rather than inlining hexes' is written for a browser/CSS pipeline that does not exist in this repo. The equivalent, honoring the SAME single-source-of-truth intent, is a new sibling TS module packages/engine-core/src/site-plan/pdf/report-chrome-tokens.ts, following the exact existing convention in template-tokens.ts (whose own header says it is 'the single place the PDF renderer resolves colour, spacing, and type from -- never hard-code a hex'). Kept as a SEPARATE file from template-tokens.ts (not merged in) because they are two different token sets for two different grounds -- the drawing/ds-industry tokens (dark-adjacent steel accent) vs the paper/print tokens -- exactly mirroring the spec's own 'print-tokens.css alongside pe-tokens.css' structure (two files, not one).

GEOMETRY CHANGE: MARGIN_TOP/MARGIN_X/MARGIN_BOTTOM (currently pt(48)/pt(46)/pt(36) = 36/34.5/27pt) move to the spec's 40/48/30px = pt(40)/pt(48)/pt(30) = 30/36/22.5pt, in render.ts (the single exported source dossier.ts/feasibility.ts/flood-drainage.ts all import from). This is page-frame geometry named explicitly in the spec's own 'Page geometry' section, not body content, and every downstream body-fit computation (page1Frame, headerRuleY, footer-band tops) is formula-driven off these constants rather than hardcoded, so body content re-flows correctly rather than silently keeping stale coordinates.

DEEP-LINK HOST DECISION (Integration Note 3 explicitly asks this be made explicit): hauska-engine's PDF code never constructs the deep-link URL today -- it only ever prints a caller-supplied `liveViewUrl` string verbatim (confirmed by full call-chain trace: parcel-terrain.ts / flood-drainage.ts routes accept an opaque liveViewUrl through zod, threaded unmodified to the draw call). One real caller (feasibility.test.ts) exercises a SHARE-token link shape (`https://smartsite.cloud/share?g=...`), not a bare parcel link -- so the engine must not unilaterally rewrite or replace a caller-supplied URL, since it may carry share/grant semantics this repo does not own. DECISION: (a) when liveViewUrl is supplied, print it verbatim as today, UNLESS its host is the confirmed-parked `smartsite.app`, in which case rewrite only the host to `smartsite.cloud` before printing (defensive, since that parked host must never reach a customer PDF -- currently zero callers do this per grep, so this is a pure safety net, not an observed bug); (b) when liveViewUrl is ABSENT -- which is ALWAYS the case for the standalone Site Plan export today, since author.ts's authorParcelSitePlanExport never threads one through emitPdfSitePlan's options at all -- the frame now builds an ABSOLUTE fallback link itself: `https://smartsite.cloud/?parcelNodeId=<percent-encoded-id>`, so every sheet always carries a working, resolvable link instead of silently omitting the footer's link slot. This requires adding an optional liveViewUrl passthrough on EmitPdfSitePlanOptions (new, currently absent) so a future caller CAN still override it; author.ts is left as-is (no caller wiring added -- out of scope beyond the frame itself; the fallback covers it either way). Absolute, not relative, per the existing (FS/FD/XR) precedent of printing full https:// URLs and per the spec's own prompt to decide explicitly rather than silently keep the relative form.
